title: Set up your plan
skipHint: Moves on without recording an answer. You can come back to it later.
saveErrorTitle: We could not save your answers
saveErrorBody: Nothing was stored and none of your answers were lost. Try again.
disclaimerContext: The figures this set-up produces come from a prototype calculator.

calculationBasis.measurementsDetail: Uses the Mifflin–St Jeor equation, which reads weight, height, age and one constant chosen by a biological parameter.
calculationBasis.bodyCompositionDetail: Uses the Katch–McArdle equation, which works from fat-free mass and needs neither height nor a biological parameter. It needs a body-fat percentage.

sedentary.label: Mostly seated
sedentary.description: A desk day, little deliberate exercise, and short walks rather than long ones.

lightly_active.label: Lightly active
lightly_active.description: On your feet for part of the day, or exercise one to three times a week.

moderately_active.label: Moderately active
moderately_active.description: Moving most days, or exercise three to five times a week.

very_active.label: Very active
very_active.description: Physical work, or hard exercise six or seven times a week.

extra_active.label: Extremely active
extra_active.description: Heavy physical work plus training, or two sessions on most days.

lose_weight.label: Lose weight
lose_weight.description: Eat below the energy that would hold you steady, at a rate you choose next.

maintain.label: Stay where I am
maintain.description: Eat at the energy that holds your weight steady, and eat better while doing it.

gain_muscle.label: Build muscle
gain_muscle.description: Eat above maintenance, with protein set per kilogram of body mass.

recomposition.label: Change my shape
recomposition.description: Hold close to maintenance with a high protein intake, trading speed for the shape of the change.

gentle.label: Gentle
gentle.description: The smallest change the goal supports. Easiest to keep to, and slowest to show.

standard.label: Steady
standard.description: The middle option, and the one most general guidance describes as sustainable.

ambitious.label: Ambitious
ambitious.description: The largest change this calculator will produce. Harder to keep to, and more likely to need a professional eye.

beginner.label: Getting started
beginner.description: Short recipes with few steps and ingredients you can buy anywhere.

confident.label: Confident
confident.description: Happy with a knife and a pan, and with a recipe that takes half an hour.

experienced.label: Experienced
experienced.description: Comfortable with longer methods, several components and unfamiliar ingredients.

home_prepared.label: I cook at home
home_prepared.description: Plans are built from recipes and a grocery list. Nothing is ordered.

kitchen_prepared.label: A kitchen cooks for me
kitchen_prepared.description: Plans are built from meals prepared by kitchens that deliver to you.

mixed.label: A mixture
mixed.description: Some meals cooked at home, some delivered — which is what most weeks actually look like.

preference.label: Preference
preference.description: A pattern you prefer. It ranks what we suggest and excludes nothing.

self_declared_medical.label: Something you told us
self_declared_medical.description: A health-related note you recorded yourself. We honour it, and it is one of the things that sends your target for professional review — but we never act on one as a clinical instruction.

dietitian_enforced.label: Set by your dietitian
dietitian_enforced.description: A restriction a qualified professional put in place. Only they can lift it, and it is shown here so you always know it exists.

allergy.label: Allergy
allergy.description: Never suggested, never planned, and never overridden — not by you, not by us, and not by a confirmation.

intolerance.label: Intolerance
intolerance.description: Filtered out by default. Because reactions depend on the amount, you can knowingly allow a particular dish.

dislike.label: Would rather avoid
dislike.description: Ranked down rather than excluded. If you ask for it, you get it.

religious.label: Observance
religious.description: Excluded as a matter of observance, not treated as a taste. You may allow a particular dish yourself; nothing else lifts it.

restrictionAuthority.confirmation: You can allow it dish by dish
restrictionAuthority.dietitian: Only your dietitian can lift this

validation.required: Please answer this before going on.
validation.acknowledge: Please confirm you have read this before going on.
validation.bodyFatNeeded: The body-composition estimate needs a body-fat percentage. Enter one, or go back and choose the estimate from measurements.
validation.mealTimesOrder: Your main meals are out of order. Put them in the order you eat them, or change which meal each one is.

introduction.title: What we ask, and what we do with it
introduction.lead: Setting up takes about five minutes. Before it starts, here is exactly what happens to what you tell us.
introduction.acknowledge: I have read this and I would like to go on.

whatWeAsk.title: What we ask for
whatWeAsk.body: Your age, height, weight and how active you are, so a published equation can estimate your energy needs. Then what you eat, what you cannot eat, and how you like to cook.

whatWeDo.title: What we do with it
whatWeDo.body: We calculate a daily energy and macronutrient target and show you every step of the arithmetic, with citations. Your answers shape the meals we suggest.

whatWeDoNot.title: What we do not do
whatWeDoNot.body: We do not diagnose anything, we do not treat anything, and we do not replace a dietitian or a doctor. Nothing here is medical advice.

notSaved.title: This prototype does not save as you go
notSaved.body: Your answers are held for this session only and stored at the end, when you save. If you close this tab part-way through, you will start again.

units.title: Which units would you like to use?
units.lead: We ask first, so every measurement after this appears in the units you actually think in.
units.noteBody: Switching units later converts what you have entered rather than clearing it.

age.title: How old are you?
age.lead: The energy equation takes a whole number of years, so that is all we ask for.
age.label: Age
age.hint: We ask for years rather than a date of birth because the calculation cannot use a day and a month, and we would rather not hold one.

calculationBasis.title: How should we estimate your resting energy?
calculationBasis.lead: There are two published equations. They ask for different things, and one of them does not need a biological parameter at all.
calculationBasis.sexLabel: Which constant should the equation use?
calculationBasis.whyBody: The Mifflin–St Jeor equation contains one constant that differs by biological sex: it adds 5 for the male form and subtracts 161 for the female form. This is a calculation input, not a question about who you are, and nothing else in the product reads it. If you would rather not answer it, choose the body-composition estimate instead.
calculationBasis.declinedBody: The Katch–McArdle equation works from fat-free mass, so we will not ask. One consequence is worth stating: the minimum-intake guard this calculator applies is also chosen by that parameter, so we apply the more cautious of the two — 1,500 kcal a day. You will see it in the working if it ever binds.

height.title: How tall are you?
height.lead: Used by the Mifflin–St Jeor equation, and to work out a body-mass index for the safety checks.
height.label: Height

weight.title: What do you weigh?
weight.lead: Used for your resting-energy estimate, and to set your protein target per kilogram of body mass.
weight.label: Weight

bodyFat.title: Do you know your body-fat percentage?
bodyFat.leadOptional: Optional. If you have a recent measurement it unlocks a more precise estimate; if not, skip it and nothing is lost.
bodyFat.leadRequired: You asked for the body-composition estimate, so this one is needed.
bodyFat.label: Body fat
bodyFat.hint: From a scan, callipers or a smart scale — whatever you have.
bodyFat.requiredBody: Without a percentage the body-composition estimate cannot run. Enter one, or go back a step and choose the estimate from measurements.
bodyFat.skipHint: We will estimate your resting energy from weight, height and age instead.
bodyFat.noBandsTitle: Why we do not offer low, medium and high
bodyFat.noBandsBody: A band would have to become a number before the equation could use it, and that number would be one nobody measured — indistinguishable, in the result, from a real measurement. We would rather you skipped it.

activity.title: How active are you, usually?
activity.lead: This describes your habitual week rather than yesterday. It is the input people most often overestimate.
activity.label: Activity level

goal.title: What are you trying to do?
goal.lead: This decides which direction your target moves from the energy that would hold you steady.
goal.label: Goal
goal.guideTitle: What each goal does to your target

pace.title: How quickly?
pace.lead: Pace decides how far your target moves from maintenance. Every option here is bounded on purpose.
pace.label: Pace
pace.safetyBody: This calculator will not produce a deficit larger than a fifth of your maintenance energy, or a surplus larger than about a seventh. Beyond those, the published evidence stops describing the extra change as the kind most people are looking for.
pace.flaggedBody: An ambitious pace with a weight-loss goal is one of the things that sends your target for a professional look. You can still choose it — we will tell you why at the end.

diet.title: How do you eat?
diet.lead: Two questions here, and they are not the same kind of thing.
diet.label: The pattern you prefer
diet.hint: A preference. It ranks what we suggest and excludes nothing.
diet.distinctionTitle: A preference is not a restriction
diet.distinctionBody: The pattern above shapes what we put in front of you first. What you tell us below excludes food outright, which is a different promise and one we keep differently.
diet.observanceLabel: Anything you do not eat as a matter of observance
diet.observanceHint: Honoured as a filter, never traded off against variety or cost. We ask about food, never about belief.

allergies.title: Are you allergic to anything?
allergies.lead: This is the one answer on this journey that nothing can override.
allergies.severityBody: Anything you name here is never suggested, never planned and never offered with a confirm-anyway control. If your allergy is severe, tell any kitchen directly as well: this interface controls what we suggest, not what happens in a kitchen.
allergies.label: The fourteen declared allergen groups
allergies.hint: These are the groups food labelling requires to be declared. Anything outside them belongs in the next two steps.
allergies.intoleranceExplainer: An intolerance is not a weak allergy. It usually depends on how much you eat, so we filter these out by default and let you allow a particular dish when you want to.

restrictions.title: Medical and dietitian restrictions
restrictions.lead: Two lists that look alike and behave completely differently. The first is yours; the second is not.
restrictions.selfDeclaredExplainer: Things you have been told to watch, or have decided to watch yourself. We record them, we honour them, and we send your target for a professional look because of them — but we never act on one as a clinical instruction.
restrictions.enforcedExplainer: Restrictions a qualified dietitian has put in place for you. They are shown here so you always know what is set and who set it.
restrictions.enforcedLoading: Checking whether a dietitian has set anything…
restrictions.enforcedErrorTitle: We could not check for dietitian restrictions
restrictions.enforcedErrorBody: This does not stop you going on, but it does mean this list may be incomplete. It is worth checking again before you rely on a plan.
restrictions.enforcedEmpty: No dietitian has set a restriction for you.
restrictions.enforcedNoNote: No note was left with this restriction.
restrictions.enforcedReadOnly: You cannot change these here. If one no longer applies, speak to the dietitian who set it.

dislikes.title: Anything you would rather not eat?
dislikes.lead: Not an allergy and not a restriction — simply things you would rather see less of.
dislikes.noteTitle: This ranks, it does not exclude
dislikes.noteBody: We will suggest these less often. If you deliberately add one to a plan, nothing will argue with you.
dislikes.label: Things to see less of

cuisines.title: Which cuisines do you enjoy?
cuisines.lead: Used to rank what we suggest first. Choosing none simply means no preference.
cuisines.label: Cuisines

budget.title: Do you have a weekly food budget?
budget.lead: Optional, and a ceiling rather than a target. Leaving it empty means no ceiling at all.
budget.label: Weekly budget
budget.hint: Roughly what you would like to spend on food in a week.
budget.noteBody: It is a hard ceiling on what a generated plan may cost, and a preference that pushes cheaper options up the list below it. It never overrides an allergy or a restriction.

cooking.title: How much time do you have to cook?
cooking.lead: On a typical day. We would rather suggest something you will actually make.
cooking.minutesHint: Per day, across all your meals.
cooking.skillLabel: How comfortable are you in the kitchen?

meals.title: How many times a day do you eat?
meals.lead: Meals and snacks are counted separately, because they are planned differently.
meals.snacksHint: Zero is a perfectly good answer.

mealTimes.title: When do you eat?
mealTimes.lead: Set the time for each one, and change what kind of meal it is if our guess is wrong.

preparation.title: Who is doing the cooking?
preparation.lead: This decides whether we plan from recipes, from kitchen meals, or from both.
preparation.label: Preparation

summary.title: Check your answers
summary.lead: Everything we now believe about how you eat. Change anything that is wrong before we calculate.
summary.previewEmpty: Answer the remaining steps and your target will appear here.
summary.previewErrorTitle: We could not calculate a target
summary.previewErrorBody: Your answers are safe. Check the numbers above and try again.
summary.reviewFlag: Will be flagged for professional review
summary.editHint: Goes back to the step that asked: {{question}}
summary.restrictionsTitle: What you can and cannot eat
summary.restrictionsLead: Seven different kinds of thing, kept apart because they behave differently. Empty ones are shown too, so you can see what we believe you have not told us.
summary.setByDietitian: Set by a dietitian, so it cannot be changed here.
summary.acknowledge: I understand these are estimates from a prototype calculator, not medical advice.
summary.acknowledgeDescription: We record this so it is clear you saw the caveat before accepting a figure.

review.title: Before you go on
review.lead: Your answers produced a target that we think a qualified person should look at. Here is exactly why.
review.warningTitle: This target has not been reviewed by anyone
review.warningBody: It came from a prototype calculator applying published general-population equations. It knows nothing about medical conditions, medication or pregnancy, and it is not medical advice.
review.reasonsEmpty: No specific reason was recorded, which is unusual — treat the figures with the same caution regardless.
review.reasonFallback: One of the safety checks in the calculator was triggered.
review.requestReview: Ask a dietitian to review this
review.requestedTitle: Your request is with a dietitian
review.requestedBody: It is on a professional's queue now. You can carry on using your plan while you wait.
review.requestErrorTitle: We could not send your request
review.requestErrorBody: Nothing was sent. You can try again, or carry on and ask later from your nutrition page.
review.acknowledge: I have read this and I understand these figures have not been reviewed.
review.acknowledgeDescription: Recorded so it is clear you saw the warning rather than passed it.
review.continueHint: Takes you to your targets. The warning stays on that page until a dietitian has reviewed them.
review.errorTitle: We could not load your target
review.errorBody: Your answers were saved. Continue to your nutrition page and the figures should be there.
